---
title: "Allow FiveMesh Cache through your firewall"
description: "Find the right port and allow Cloudflare IP ranges so FiveMesh Cache can download files from your FiveM server."
icon: "shield-check"
---

If your players get resource download errors while your FiveM server is still online, your firewall or hosting provider's DDoS protection may be blocking FiveMesh Cache.

FiveMesh Cache downloads a file from your server when that file is not already cached. These requests use Cloudflare's network, so your server must accept connections from Cloudflare on its **resource download port**.

## What is a firewall?

A firewall controls which network connections are allowed to reach your server. Your hosting provider may have a **network firewall or DDoS protection** in its control panel, and your server may have another firewall in Windows or Linux.

An **IP allowlist** is a set of addresses that your firewall is told to accept. For FiveMesh Cache, you can allow Cloudflare's published IP ranges.

## Which settings should I use?

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Direction | **Inbound** (connections to your server) |
| Action | **Allow** |
| Protocol | **TCP** |
| Source IP addresses | All current Cloudflare IPv4 and IPv6 ranges at [cloudflare.com/ips](https://www.cloudflare.com/ips/) |
| Destination | Your FiveM server's public resource download endpoint |
| Destination port | The port shown in **Cache** > **Settings** for your origin |

The default FiveM port is `30120`, but your server may use a different port. If your origin is `http://play.example.com:30120`, allow incoming **TCP 30120**. If you use a reverse proxy with `https://play.example.com`, the external port may be **443** instead.

<Warning>
  These IP ranges are shared by Cloudflare customers; they do not identify FiveMesh alone. Keep your existing authentication and DDoS protection. **Do not disable your firewall, open every port, or block all other FiveM traffic.** Allowing Cloudflare traffic must not prevent players from connecting normally.
</Warning>

## Find your origin port

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open FiveMesh Cache settings">
    In the [FiveMesh dashboard](https://app.fivemesh.io), select your registered server and open **Cache** > **Settings**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Check the origin URL">
    Note the hostname and port of the **origin**, not the public `cache.fivemesh.io` URL. An explicit `:30120` means port `30120`. Without an explicit port, HTTP normally uses `80` and HTTPS uses `443`.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Check where the firewall is configured">
    Look in your game hosting panel for **Firewall**, **Network**, **Security**, or **DDoS protection**. You may also need to update the Windows or Linux firewall on the server itself.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Game hosting panel or provider firewall

Your hosting provider's interface may look different, but the required rule is the same.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the firewall or DDoS protection settings">
    Select the public IP address or FiveM server that receives resource downloads.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Create an allow rule">
    Set **Inbound**, **Allow**, **TCP** and the origin's **destination port**. For the **source IP**, add the Cloudflare networks from [cloudflare.com/ips](https://www.cloudflare.com/ips/). Include IPv4 and IPv6 if your origin is reachable over both.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Save and repeat where needed">
    Some panels need one rule per IP range. Save all ranges, then check for a second firewall or DDoS ruleset upstream of the game server. If you host multiple FiveM servers on different fileserver ports, repeat for each port.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Info>
  If you cannot find firewall settings or the host blocks Cloudflare traffic in its DDoS layer, contact the hosting provider. A Windows or Linux rule cannot override a block applied before traffic reaches your machine.
</Info>

## Windows Server firewall

You need administrator access to your Windows Server.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open Windows Defender Firewall">
    Press **Win + R**, type `wf.msc`, and open **Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Create a custom inbound rule">
    Select **Inbound Rules** > **New Rule** > **Custom**. Choose **All programs**. Under **Protocol and Ports**, select **TCP** and set the **Local port** to the origin port from FiveMesh Cache.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Add Cloudflare source ranges">
    Under **Scope** > **Remote IP address**, choose **These IP addresses**. Add each applicable IPv4 and IPv6 range from [cloudflare.com/ips](https://www.cloudflare.com/ips/).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Allow and save">
    Choose **Allow the connection**, select the appropriate network profiles, and name the rule something like **FiveMesh Cache - TCP 30120**. Confirm the rule is enabled.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Linux with UFW

If your server uses UFW, allow each Cloudflare CIDR range on the correct TCP port. For example, for TCP port `30120`, one IPv4 range would be:

~~~bash
sudo ufw allow from 173.245.48.0/20 to any port 30120 proto tcp
~~~

This command is **only one example range**. Repeat it using **every current applicable IPv4 and IPv6 range** from [cloudflare.com/ips](https://www.cloudflare.com/ips/), and replace `30120` if your origin uses another port.

Check the resulting rules with:

~~~bash
sudo ufw status
~~~

<Warning>
  If UFW is not already enabled, do not enable it blindly on a remote server. First verify that your SSH, management and player connections will remain accessible.
</Warning>

## Ask your hosting provider for help

If your host manages the firewall, send them this message:

> Hello, I use FiveMesh Cache for my FiveM server. Could you allow inbound **TCP** connections from all Cloudflare IPv4 and IPv6 ranges listed at https://www.cloudflare.com/ips/ to my resource download endpoint **HOSTNAME:PORT**? Please check the network firewall and DDoS protection rules. This is for FiveMesh Cache to fetch uncached resources. Please keep normal player connectivity intact.

Replace **HOSTNAME:PORT** with the origin endpoint in **Cache** > **Settings**.

## Verify that it works

1. Save the new firewall rules.
2. Trigger a download of a resource that is **not already cached**. A successful Cache HIT does not test connectivity to your origin.
3. Check **Cache** > **Analytics** for origin errors and confirm resource downloads succeed.
4. If it still fails, check the port, the TCP protocol, IPv4/IPv6 ranges, and any firewall or DDoS protection managed by your hosting provider.

You normally do not need to restart FiveM or purge your entire cache just to apply firewall changes.

If the issue continues, open a [support ticket](https://discord.gg/wBJamWETxr) with your hosting provider, registered server ID, origin hostname and port, and the error you see. Do not share your `adhesive_cdnKey` or other secrets.

<Info>
  This allowlist applies to **FiveMesh Cache HTTP origin requests**. Do not assume it applies to other FiveMesh products, database backups, or Cloudflare Containers.
</Info>
